domain: Safeguarding of living heritage and craft transmission — guild apprenticeship and the chef-d'oeuvre, iemoto lineage, living-human-treasure designation, and Ise Jingu's shikinen sengu twenty-year ritual reconstruction: the inventory-versus-transmission distinction, the doctrine that documenting a practice is not safeguarding it, folklorization when a catalogue begins prescribing the practice it described, and works made for an occasion that are complete when the occasion ends
axioms: Documenting a practice is not safeguarding it; an inventory of a tradition's products grows most impressively exactly while its transmission is failing, because inventory is cheap and transmission is not.
An artifact records the outcome of a making, never the conditions of the making; whatever the maker knew and never had to state is absent from the artifact and cannot be recovered from it afterwards.

Some works are made for an occasion and are complete when the occasion ends; storing them as though they were meant to persist misrepresents what they are and offers them for uses they were never fit for.

Preservation by periodic remaking transmits capability; preservation by storage transmits only form — and a tradition that stops remaking loses the ability to remake long before anyone notices the loss.

A practice that is catalogued and rated changes: once a register of recognised forms exists and is consulted before making, makers begin producing what the register recognises, and the narrowing looks from inside like consolidation.
Transmission is proven only by a successor performing the work unaided; a lineage with no successor who has actually done the thing is a claim about continuity, not continuity.
The threat to a living tradition is rarely the destruction of its objects; it is the disappearance of the occasions that required them, which leaves the objects intact and inert.
primitives: living practice vs recorded output (a review generating a lens against a live target and heat state, vs the fd-* file it leaves behind)
the occasion (the specific review, round, target, prior-round findings and sibling anti-overlap contract that required this lens and no other)
tacit conditions of making (what the generating agent knew but no field holds — the absent fusion lineage in frontmatter as the measured sample)
ephemeral vs durable work (a -fusion-N lens made for one round, or a sibling shaped by its contract with the others, vs a lens meant to be reused)
inventory (the census — 2,881 + 1,628 agents, 671 + 402 specs — and completeness as the success measure)
safeguarding measure vs inventory metric (evidence that a review got better, vs a count of records held and files swept)
periodic reconstruction as preservation (cheap well-aimed regeneration keeping only the seed of the occasion — the counter-design none of the five forks weighed)
folklorization (the embodies match against the curated definitions, and the reuse seam shaping what flux-gen writes next)
bearer (zklw as the sole site of harvest, merge and embedding; the single operator hand-porting graph.py)
successor and re-derivation (what a returning operator, the other machine, or a fresh session could rebuild from the repository alone)
failure_mode: Indifferent to mechanism: will not evaluate schema correctness, merge semantics, ranking math, embedding choices, or whether the JS port of graph.py is right — every one of those can be broken and this lens will not notice.
Romanticizes remaking, and can argue against storage as such; will undervalue the cases where a cached artifact is simply correct and regenerating it is pure waste.
Cannot check a quantity — no denominator, threshold, dimension or uncertainty claim will be examined, so a design whose numbers are wrong but whose transmission story is sound passes clean.
Prone to the unfalsifiable: 'tacit knowledge is lost' is easy to assert and hard to act on, and findings can drift into lament unless forced to name the missing field or absent step.
Blind to the two-machine boundary as an availability or consistency surface; sees it only as a question of who may perform the work, so split-brain in the ordinary sense is invisible to it.

Underweights cost: will propose successor runs, re-derivations and recorded occasions whose overhead a single-operator personal registry cannot carry, and has no instinct for when the ceremony exceeds the asset.
